entries.application: Fourier series representation of a periodic signal
equations: x(t) = Σₖ cₖ exp(i k ω₀ t)
cₖ = (1/T₀)∫₀ᵀ⁰ x(t) exp(-i k ω₀ t) dt
assumptions: Periodic signal with suitable integrability
coefficient convention and interval are fixed.
entries.initial_conditions: Specify one full period or equivalent periodic extension.
entries.boundary_conditions: Not applicable as a spatial boundary-value model; declare finite observation interval, window, or probability sample space as appropriate.
entries.validity_regime: Harmonic representation of periodic signals; convergence at discontinuities may be to midpoint values under standard conditions.
entries.intuition: A repeating pattern decomposes into harmonics at integer multiples of its base frequency.
limitations: Convergence depends on regularity and chosen summation interpretation
Finite truncation introduces approximation and Gibbs oscillations
validation: Reconstruct test signals from coefficients
Check Parseval identity and convergence for smooth and discontinuous examples

entries.application: Quantization and uniform quantization noise model
equations: σ_q² = Δ²/12 under the ideal uniform-error model
assumptions: No overload
ideal rounding
quantization error treated as uniform and sufficiently decorrelated when invoking Δ²/12.
entries.initial_conditions: Input range and quantizer step are specified.
entries.boundary_conditions: Not applicable as a spatial boundary-value model; declare finite observation interval, window, or probability sample space as appropriate.
entries.validity_regime: Uniform scalar quantizer; variance formula is a model under stated assumptions, not universal truth.
entries.intuition: Finite precision maps a continuum of amplitudes to discrete levels.
limitations: Overload invalidates the simple noise model
Error may be signal-correlated, especially for low-level or periodic inputs
validation: Enumerate quantization error over a bounded range
Monte Carlo variance test with explicit input assumptions and seed
uncertainty: Reference voltage, offset, gain, and converter nonlinearity
